previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy and GJ tube dependence, and a history of osteonecrosis was admitted for fever. Evaluation revealed leukocytosis and a urinary tract infection caused by resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with a 7-day course of IV cefepime, with improvement in symptoms and labs. A CT scan identified a 6 mm stone in the right ureter, which may contribute to recurrent infections, prompting a urology referral. His GJ tube was exchanged during admission due to malposition. Chronic conditions, including HIV, seizures, and right hip pain from osteonecrosis, were managed with ongoing medications. He remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged back to his extended care facility with follow-up plans.
